faq.a: Lejla is associated with the Arabic form لَيْلَى, whose core sense is lejla; night (balkan form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Lejla?
faq.a: Lejla is associated with Arabic. Lejla is the Bosnian form of Arabic لَيْلَى (Laylā), associated with the sense 'night'.
Yes — the underlying form لَيْلَى is Arabic.
Lejla can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Lejla should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Laylā is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.a: In Urdu, Lejla is rendered لیلیٰ and carries the sense لیلیٰ، رات.

faq.q: What does Lejla mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Lejla is rendered لیلا and carries the sense لیلا، شب.
A romanized syllable approximation is lej-la. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Lejla?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Lejla, lejla. Script forms are ليلا, لَيْلَى, لیلا, لیلیٰ, लैला.

faq.q: Is Lejla a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
